description: Single-variable and introductory multivariable calculus with differential equations, taught with R and MATLAB alongside the pen so that every technique is also computed and plotted. Taught to the depth of a full first-year calculus sequence.
outcomes: Compute limits and derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions and apply them to rates, optimisation and curve sketching.
Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals by substitution, parts, partial fractions and trigonometric methods, and apply them to area, volume and average value.
Approximate integrals numerically with the trapezoidal and Simpson rules and bound the error.
Differentiate functions of several variables, find gradients, and locate and classify extrema.
Set up and evaluate double and triple integrals for areas, volumes and masses.
Solve first-order differential equations analytically and numerically and model growth, decay and cooling.

units.title: Functions, limits and continuity
topics: Review of functions, graphs, polynomials, rational, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Limits: intuition, one-sided limits, limit laws, squeeze theorem; limits at infinity
Continuity, types of discontinuity, intermediate value theorem
Plotting functions and estimating limits in R and MATLAB

units.title: Differential calculus
topics: Derivative as a limit, as slope and as rate of change; differentiability
Rules: power, product, quotient, chain; implicit and logarithmic differentiation
Derivatives of trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic functions
Applications: related rates, linear approximation, l'Hopital's rule
Mean value theorem; increasing and decreasing functions; concavity and curve sketching
Optimisation: maximising profit for a market stall, minimising material for a tank
Newton's method and symbolic differentiation in software

units.title: Integral calculus
topics: Antiderivatives and the indefinite integral; Riemann sums and the definite integral
Fundamental theorem of calculus
Substitution, integration by parts, trigonometric integrals and substitutions
Partial fractions and integration of rational functions
Improper integrals
Applications: area between curves, volumes of revolution, arc length, average value, work

units.title: Approximate integration
topics: Midpoint, trapezoidal and Simpson's rules
Error bounds and choosing the number of subintervals
Implementing the rules in R and MATLAB and comparing with built-in integrators
Taylor and Maclaurin series; using series to approximate integrals

units.title: Partial differentiation
topics: Functions of two and three variables; level curves and surfaces
Partial derivatives, higher-order partials, Clairaut's theorem
Tangent planes, differentials and the chain rule for several variables
Gradient and directional derivatives
Local extrema, second-derivative test, Lagrange multipliers

units.title: Multiple integrals and volumes
topics: Double integrals over rectangles and general regions; changing the order of integration
Double integrals in polar coordinates
Triple integrals; cylindrical and spherical coordinates
Applications: volume, mass, centre of mass, surface area

units.title: First-order differential equations
topics: Modelling with differential equations; direction fields
Separable and linear first-order equations; integrating factors; exact equations
Applications: population growth and logistic models, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling, mixing problems, RC circuits
Euler's method and Runge-Kutta in R and MATLAB; comparing numeric and exact solutions
A glimpse of second-order equations and oscillation
